To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the coal-bearing succession of the Mary Lee coal member of the Pottsville Formation in the Black Warrior basin is a parasequence set of the highstand systems tract of the genetic sequence of the Pottsvillian sequence.
the Mary Lee coal-bearing strata are composed of a genetic sequence that includes seven parasequence sets.
the Mary Lee coal is a highstand parasequence set that formed during the late stage of a transgressive-regressive cycle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of sequence and genetic concepts to Carboniferus coal-bearing strata, and the development of a genetic model for the Black Warrior basin.

the identification of genetic stratigraphies, parasequences, and sequence boundaries within the Mary Lee coal-bearing strata, and the evaluation of the utility of these concepts for Carboniferous stratal studies in general.
the identification, correlation, and evaluation of the coal bearing strata of the Mary Lee coal field, located in the Black Warrior basin of north-eastern Alabama, USA (Fig. 1).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the concepts of genetic stratigraphy and sequence stratigraphy are complementary, not competitive, approaches to the study of stratigraphy.
the genetic stratigraphic framework provides a more detailed and comprehensive interpretation of the coal-bearing succession in the Black Warrior basin.
the genetic and sequence stratigraphies are complementary.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the concepts of both genetic stratigraphy and sequence stratigraphy have been successfully applied to the Carboniferous stratal succession in the Black Warrior basin.
the genetic stratigraphic model has provided the framework for the recognition of the parasequence sets.

the genetic stratigraphic model provides a framework that is useful for identifying and describing facies, but that the sequence stratigraphic model is more useful in the identification and interpretation of the stratigraphic record.
The main takeaway from our work is that
both approaches are useful in understanding the stratigraphy of the coal-bearing succession.
the genetic stratigraphic approach provides a more robust framework for the evaluation of coal-bearing strata than does the sequence stratigraphic approach.
genetic stratigraphic analysis can provide an excellent framework for the recognition of sequence stratigraphic components.
